A small plaque ______ from mammoth ivory, dating from 30,000 BCE, is thought to have been carved by prehistoric humans to represent the constellation Orion.
exp: 문장의 동사는 is thought이므로 빈칸에는 주어 A small plaque를 뒤에서 꾸미는 말이 와야 한다. 판은 매머드 상아로 "만들어진" 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 made가 알맞다. makes와 was made는 동사가 하나 더 생겨 틀리고, to make는 능동이라 뜻이 맞지 않는다.

Minji Kim (10:12 am): Hi! How many are in your group?
James Mayer (10:13 am): 8. I think we’ll need a large van.
Minji Kim (10:13 am): ______?
James Mayer (10:15 am): Riverside Hotel. Is it far from the airport?
Minji Kim (10:15 am): No, it’s only a 5 minute drive.
James Mayer (10:17 am): Great! Can you pick us up tomorrow at 10 am? Gate 7.
Minji Kim (10:17 am): Sure! See you tomorrow.
opts: Do you need a smaller car
How long are you staying in Korea
When will you pick up your luggage
exp: 빈칸 뒤에서 James가 "Riverside Hotel"이라고 목적지를 답하고 공항에서 먼지 묻고 있으므로, 빈칸은 "일행이 어디로 가십니까"라는 질문이어야 한다. 더 작은 차, 한국 체류 기간, 짐 찾는 때를 묻는 말에는 호텔 이름으로 답할 수 없다.

NoRatVctr (https://noratvectors.com)

(A) ______

The Vector Control Program inspects and treats disease vectors from rats. (Vectors are living organisms that can transfer diseases to people.)

Process for our rat program:
■ Make a service request through 311.
■ Our team will come to your property to do an assessment.
■ If you see active signs (droppings, hairs, tracks) and you wish to have the property treated, we will ask you to sign a Release of Liability form for us to service your property.

■ No dog waste
■ No bird seed
■ No overgrown yards
■ No trash/debris

exp: 글은 Springfield 보건 당국의 Vector Control Program이 쥐를 점검·처리해 주는 절차와 조건을 안내하므로 "Springfield의 매개체 방제 서비스"가 제목으로 알맞다. 매개체가 집에 퍼지는 과정, 스스로 식별하는 법, 방제업자 자격을 얻는 법은 글에 나오지 않는다.

q:
윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

HHWnever (https://hhwnever.com)

Household Hazardous Waste

Leftover household products that can catch fire or explode under certain circumstances are considered household hazardous waste (HHW). Although it depends on your local solid waste agency or recycling facility, some examples include pesticides, paints, light bulbs, batteries, and nail polish. These products require special care when you dispose of them. HHW may be dangerous to people and bad for the environment if they are poured down the drain, dumped on the ground, or thrown out with __regular__ trash.

What you can do:
▪ Try to reduce your purchases of these products, and look for alternative, non-hazardous products.
▪ When you need to dispose of these products, look for special collection events in your community or permanent collection centers.
▪ If you have to dispose of HHW, first check with your local waste management agency to learn what rules apply in your community.
opts: to promote the safe disposal of HHW
to show how HHW is managed at collection centers
to inform how to distinguish HHW from regular trash
to introduce local agencies dealing with HHW
exp: 가정용 유해 폐기물은 아무렇게나 버리면 사람과 환경에 해로우니 덜 사고, 수거 행사나 수거 센터를 이용하고, 지역 규정을 확인하라고 권하는 글이므로 안전한 처리를 장려하는 것이 목적이다. 수거 센터의 관리 방식, 일반 쓰레기와 구별하는 법, 담당 기관 소개는 글의 중심 내용이 아니다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.

Personality typing is a system of categorizing people (1) __depending__ on how they think and act in certain situations―but there are clear differences between different personality type systems and what they can tell you about yourself. The Myers and Briggs personality system and the Enneagram of Personality are two leading personality typing systems (2) __that__ are used around the world. Both systems help people (3) __gains__ a better insight into their career possibilities, the dynamics of their relationships, the working patterns of their employees and even their own thought patterns. Some personality typologists prefer (4) __to use__ one system over the other but the two systems are often used together. Each has their own strengths and weaknesses.
exp: help는 "help + 목적어 + (to) 동사원형" 꼴로 쓰므로 gains가 아니라 gain 또는 to gain이어야 한다. depending on은 "~에 따라"라는 뜻의 분사 표현, that은 systems를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사, prefer to use는 to부정사를 목적어로 취한 것이어서 모두 옳다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.

Moltbook is a site (1) __where__ the AI agents―bots built by humans―can post and interact with each other. It is designed to look like Reddit, (2) __with__ subreddits on different topics and upvoting*. On 2 February the platform stated it had more than 1.5 million AI agents signed up to the service. Humans are allowed, but only (3) __as__ observers. Moltbook was developed in the wake of Moltbot, a free and open-source AI bot that can act as an automated agent for users―doing the mundane tasks assigned to it such as reading, summarising and responding to emails, organising a calendar or (4) __book__ a table at a restaurant.

* upvoting: ‘좋아요’ 누르기
exp: such as 뒤에 reading, summarising and responding, organising이 동명사로 나열되고 or로 이어지므로 마지막도 같은 꼴인 booking이어야 한다(병렬 구조). where는 a site를 선행사로 하고 뒤에 완전한 절이 오는 관계부사, with는 "~을 갖춘"이라는 전치사, as는 "~로서"라는 전치사로 모두 옳다.

q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Giraffes may all look identical to us. But none has exactly the same markings―and certain patterns, especially large, round patches, can boost their chances of survival before they turn 4 months old. Biologists can’t decide why giraffes evolved patches. David Lee at the Nature Institute in South Carolina and his colleagues examined 258 wild baby Masai giraffes in Tanzania for clues to the impact of patches on the animals. They found that calves with fewer, larger spots had a 17 percent higher chance of survival than those with more, smaller spots. They also found that those with more round spots had a 27 percent higher survival rate than those with elliptical* spots.

* elliptical: 타원형의
opts: the unique ways to raise baby giraffes in Tanzania
different survival rates of baby giraffes by region
the relationship between baby giraffes’ spots and survival rates
scientific methods to conduct research on giraffes’ calves
exp: 무늬가 적고 크거나 둥근 새끼 기린의 생존율이 더 높았다는 연구 결과를 소개하므로 주제는 "새끼 기린의 무늬와 생존율의 관계"이다. 기린을 기르는 방법, 지역별 생존율 차이, 연구 방법 자체는 글의 중심 내용이 아니다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

In the face of significant education policy challenges such as emerging skills shortages and the need for teaching and learning innovation, schools are seeking ways to enhance school effectiveness.

(A) By assisting teachers to better understand student learning processes and education policies, schools can improve teacher effectiveness and address the looming teacher shortage resulting from retiring baby-boomers and staff who leave when their term contracts end.
(B) Schools should then effectively and efficiently convey this vital information to teachers in a way that maintains the teaching quality.
(C) To survive these shortages, schools must put processes in place before teachers leave and their pedagogical knowledge leaves with them. Because of the ageing workforce, it is critical to have effective succession planning in place to capture this knowledge.
exp: 주어진 글의 "학교 효과성을 높일 방법"을 (A)가 교사 지원과 다가오는 교사 부족 문제로 이어 받는다. (C)의 these shortages는 (A)의 teacher shortage를 가리키고, (B)의 this vital information은 (C)에서 붙잡아 두어야 한다고 한 지식(this knowledge)을 가리키므로 (A)－(C)－(B) 순서이다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

The gap probably had more to do with each school’s resources than with a student’s daily ration of chocolate cereal.

We’ve all heard that kids who eat breakfast do better in school. ( (1) ) It makes sense; it’s hard to focus on an empty stomach. ( (2) ) But despite their best attempts, researchers haven’t been able to pinpoint why breakfast aids learning―if that’s even the case. ( (3) ) A study of elementary school students found that, in some schools, kids behaved better after they ate breakfast; in other schools, they acted worse. ( (4) ) Students at well-equipped schools behave better regardless of their diet.
exp: 주어진 문장의 The gap(그 차이)은 어떤 학교에서는 아침을 먹은 뒤 행동이 좋아지고 다른 학교에서는 나빠졌다는 연구 결과를 가리키므로 그 바로 뒤인 (4)에 들어가야 한다. 또 "학교의 자원과 더 관련이 있다"는 내용이 마지막 문장의 "시설이 잘 갖춰진 학교의 학생들은 식사와 상관없이 더 잘 행동한다"로 자연스럽게 이어진다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Films, like literary works, are powerful instruments of education. (1) __On a simpler level, English language movies can be used in classrooms as a vehicle for teaching the English language.__ (2) __However, the animated film Future Galaxy deals with social issues from a historical perspective.__ (3) __But on a higher level, movies can be used as prisms through which one can learn how to understand, analyze and “read” complex aspects of the world humans have constructed and deconstructed in diverse issues in cultural, social, political, and economic spheres.__ (4) __Perhaps not most, but many Hollywood movies can be an insightful source to teach not only American culture, but also socio-economic-political-historical facets in content-based classes.__
exp: 글은 영화가 교육 도구로 쓰이는 방식을 "단순한 수준(영어 교육)"과 "더 높은 수준(세상을 이해하고 분석하는 틀)"으로 나누어 설명한다. (2)는 특정 애니메이션 영화가 무엇을 다루는지 말할 뿐이어서, On a simpler level과 But on a higher level로 이어지는 대비의 흐름을 끊는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Recently, it has been demonstrated in a series of ingenious experiments that we even perceive colors through ______. There are radical variations in the way languages carve up the spectrum of visible light; for example, green and blue are distinct colors in English but are considered shades of the same color in many languages. And it turns out that the colors that our language routinely obliges us to treat as distinct can refine our purely visual sensitivity to certain color differences in reality, so that our brains are trained to exaggerate the distance between shades of color if these have different names in our language. As strange as it may sound, our experience of a Chagall painting actually depends to some extent on whether our language has a word for blue.
opts: the lens of our mother tongue
exp: 언어가 색을 어떻게 나누어 부르느냐에 따라 실제 색 차이에 대한 시각적 민감도까지 달라진다는 내용이므로, 우리는 "모국어라는 렌즈"를 통해 색을 지각한다는 말이 알맞다. 가시광선의 반사, 색조의 비교, 여러 언어 사용자 사이의 의사소통은 글의 요지와 관계가 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Most of us put a lot of stock in what scientists tell us because we know that scientists reach their conclusions by gathering and analyzing facts. If someone asked you why you believe that smoking is bad and jogging is good, or that the earth is round and the galaxy is flat, you would point to the facts. You might need to explain that you do not personally know the facts to which you are pointing, but that you do know that at some time in the past, a bunch of very earnest people in white lab coats went out and watched the world, wrote down what they looked into, analyzed what they wrote down, and then told the rest of us what to believe. Scientists are credible because they draw conclusions from ______, and ever since the empiricists trumped the dogmatists* and became the kings of ancient Greek medicine, westerners have had a special reverence for conclusions that are based on things they can see.

* dogmatist: 교조주의자
exp: 과학자들은 세상을 지켜보고(watched the world) 기록하고 분석해 결론을 내리며, 서양인은 "볼 수 있는 것에 바탕을 둔 결론"을 존중해 왔다고 했으므로 빈칸에는 observation(관찰)이 알맞다. intuition(직관), inspiration(영감), speculation(추측)은 사실을 모으고 본다는 내용과 반대된다.
